notes: Full HTTP-tier investigation (Shopify store; robots.txt has no Claude-specific disallow, standard crawl-trap blocks only). Fetched robots.txt, sitemap.xml, sitemap_collections_1.xml (185 collections total), sitemap_products_1.xml + sitemap_products_2.xml (~1933 SKUs, all handles), and the homepage. Searched the full collection list and the full product-handle list for diwali/toran/diya/rangoli/christmas/xmas/santa/holi/rakhi/raksha/valentine/easter/halloween/thanksgiving/new-year keywords: ZERO product handles anywhere in the catalog reference any holiday. Candidate holiday-named collections found in the live sitemap: diwali-gifts (73 products), rakshabandhan-gifts (51), valentines-day-gifts (23), fathers-day-gifts (20), gifts-for-mother (30), christmas-gifts (0, empty), festive-decor-gifts (0, empty), plus generic non-holiday-specific 'festive-*' collections (festive-tableware 11, festive-table 3, festive-look 3, festive-gifts 73, festive-gifts-1 2, festive-hosting 39, festive-clothing-collection 129) and gifts-for-rituals (74). Content-sampled every one of these via /products.json: all contain the SAME generic pool of everyday SKUs (scented candles, ceramic tea/dinner sets, napkins, cake stands, string lights, digital gift cards, kaftans/tops) with NO occasion-specific design/motif (no diyas, torans, rangoli, Lakshmi/Ganesh imagery, ornaments, wreaths, rakhi threads, hearts, etc). Proved this decisively: diwali-gifts and the generic (non-holiday) festive-gifts collection are 100% IDENTICAL product sets (same 73 handles, verified with diff). rakshabandhan-gifts/valentines-day-gifts/fathers-day-gifts/gifts-for-mother each share 5-16 of their SKUs with diwali-gifts too - proving these are marketing 'gift guide' landing pages built from a shared generic-gifting SKU pool and relabeled per occasion, not genuine occasion-specific taxonomy/product lines (explicitly disqualified by rule 1: gift-guide pages are not genuine PLPs). christmas-gifts and festive-decor-gifts are additionally empty (0 products) regardless. Also found and disproved a red herring: the homepage HTML contains a leftover content block (with ellementry.com CDN image URLs, evidently copy-pasted from a sister-brand's blog/theme snippet) linking to /collections/rakhi-gifting, /collections/new-year-gifts, /collections/valentines-day, /collections/rakhi-dooj-gifts - tested all four directly and every one 404s on freedomtree.in; they are not real pages on this site. Non-holiday 'seasonal-looking' collections were also checked and excluded as out of scope: monsoon-collection, spring-summer-collection, autumn-winter-collection (fashion/weather seasons, not holidays), zodiac (astrology, not a holiday). No Holi, Easter, Halloween, Thanksgiving, or generic New Year collection exists anywhere in the sitemap or product catalog. Conclusion: after thorough investigation including particular focus on Diwali, Freedom Tree has no genuine seasonal/holiday product category - only generic gift-guide marketing pages reusing ordinary catalog SKUs under holiday-flavored URLs, which the task rules explicitly disqualify.
